recipes.name: Pan Fried Gnocchi with Pumpkin & Spinach
ingredients: 50g (3 tbsp) butter (, salted (unsalted also ok, just add more salt))
instructions: Roast pumpkin - Preheat oven to 200°C/390°F (180°C fan-forced). Place pumpkin in a large bowl, drizzle with oil, sprinkle with salt and pepper. Toss to coat, spread out on tray and bake for 20 - 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and soft inside. (Start the gnocchi 10 minutes into the roasting time).

Cook gnocchi - Bring a large pot of water to the boil, add a good pinch of salt. Cook gnocchi according to packet directions (usually ~2 minutes), or until gnocchi pops to the surface of the water (see video). SCOOP OUT a large mug of cooking water, then drain gnocchi well.
Toast gnocchi - Place butter in a skillet then put on the stove over medium high heat. Once it foams, add gnocchi immediately. Stir, turn up the heat to high, then leave to cook for about 30 seconds.
Add garlic and sage, then stir / toss for no longer than 1 1/2 minutes (i.e. 2 minutes in total - see Note 2) until gnocchi is golden on both sides.

Make sauce - Add 1/2 cup of gnocchi cooking water and toss - the water will evaporate quickly and thicken into a glaze-like sauce that coats the gnocchi (the starch in the water + butter thickens when combined).

Finish - Then add the pumpkin and spinach and stir quickly until the spinach is just wilted, adding a small splash of the gnocchi cooking water if it looks like the sauce has evaporated (it hasn't, it's just thickened and is coating the gnocchi so extra water will magically recreate the sauce). Taste and add salt and pepper to taste (saltiness of gnocchi depends on brands, so important to try). Toss then serve immediately with freshly grated parmesan.

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Gnocchi from the fridge is fresh gnocchi that is made with natural potato, and is my preference. Gnocchi from the pasta aisle will work too but it does taste slightly different as it’s made from reconstituted potato (a little like powdered mashed potato). 2. Over toasting gnocchi – If you pan fry gnocchi for too long, it becomes chewy inside which is not very nice! That’s why I limit the pan frying to 2 minutes. Leftovers – Gnocchi is best served freshly made but leftovers will keep for 3 days. Save a little of the cloudy cooking water to loosen, you can recreate the lovely butter sauce (add a slosh, microwave to reheat, mix gently). Nutrition per serving.
